root_cause.text: In erofs file-backed read I/O completion, a short read due to signal interruption is handled by zero-filling the remaining bio bytes and marking all folios as uptodate, instead of treating the incomplete read as an I/O error, which can lead to stale or incorrect data being considered valid.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "For file-backed mount, IO requests are handled by vfs_iocb_iter_read(). However, it can be interrupted by SIGKILL, returning the number of bytes actually copied. Unused folios in bio are unexpectedly marked as uptodate." The patch shows that the previous code used `bio_advance` and `zero_fill_bio` on short reads, while the fix replaces that with `ret = -EIO` to fail the bio.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states: "For file-backed mount, IO requests are handled by vfs_iocb_iter_read(). However, it can be interrupted by SIGKILL, returning the number of bytes actually copied. Unused folios in bio are unexpectedly marked as uptodate." The patch shows that the previous code used `bio_advance` and `zero_fill_bio` on short reads, while the fix replaces that with `ret = -EIO` to fail the bio.

candidates.rationale: Obtains the request structure, required for the subsequent short-read handling logic. While not directly vulnerable, it is part of the same completion path.
Declares the iterator used to walk all folios in the bio. This is a necessary step before marking folios uptodate.
This condition incorrectly treats a short read (e.g., due to signal interruption) as a non-error. Instead of propagating an I/O error, it allows the zero-fill to proceed.
Advances the bio past the successfully read bytes; prepares the bio for zero-filling the remaining part, contributing to the incomplete read being mishandled.
Fills the rest of the bio with zeroes, which masks the I/O short read and allows stale or uninitialized data to be treated as valid when folios are later marked uptodate.
Checks whether the bio completion callback is set; if false, the code proceeds to iterate folios and mark them uptodate. This guards the faulty marking path.
Starts a loop over every folio in the (possibly zero-filled) bio. This loop is the mechanism by which each folio is subsequently marked uptodate, completing the vulnerability.

Debug assertion within the folio loop; while not affecting correctness, it is part of the same code block that is intended to set folio uptodate (not shown here), confirming the vulnerable marking execution.
